relationship.statement: A pendulum swings slower when its string is longer or its release angle is wide, where sin(theta) drops below theta. Changing the bob mass scales the restoring force and inertia together, leaving the swing angle and period unchanged.
assumptions: Earth gravity is held fixed at 9.81 m/s^2.
The rod is rigid and massless with no air drag or pivot friction.
Reference pendulum is fixed at 1.0 m length, 1.0 kg mass, and 15 deg start angle.

quantities.label: String length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the pivot to the center of the test pendulum bob.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Initial angle from vertical where the test pendulum is released from rest.

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the test pendulum bob.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Gravitational acceleration held constant at 9.81 m/s^2.

quantities.label: Test period
quantities.meaning: Time for one full back-and-forth swing of the test pendulum.

quantities.label: Reference period
quantities.meaning: Time for one full swing of the fixed 1.0 m, 1.0 kg, 15 deg reference pendulum.

quantities.label: Peak restoring force
quantities.meaning: Largest tangential pull m*g*sin(theta_0) acting on the test bob at release.

quantities.label: Peak acceleration
quantities.meaning: Largest tangential acceleration g*sin(theta_0) of the test bob, independent of mass.

quantities.label: Test swing angle
quantities.meaning: Angle of the test pendulum from straight down at time t.

quantities.label: Reference angle
quantities.meaning: Angle of the reference pendulum from straight down at time t.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var g = 9.81; var L = inputs.length; var m = inputs.mass; var degToRad = Math.PI / 180; var theta0 = inputs.start_angle * degToRad; function solvePendulum(len, th0, time) { var k = Math.sin(th0 * 0.5); var a = [1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]; var b = [Math.cos(th0 * 0.5), 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]; var c = [k, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]; var i; for (i = 0; i < 5; i++) { a[i + 1] = 0.5 * (a[i] + b[i]); b[i + 1] = Math.sqrt(a[i] * b[i]); c[i + 1] = 0.5 * (a[i] - b[i]); } var aN = a[5]; var K = Math.PI / (2 * aN); var omega0 = Math.sqrt(g / len); var period = (4 * K) / omega0; var w = K - omega0 * time; var phi = 32 * aN * w; for (i = 5; i >= 1; i--) { var ratio = c[i] / a[i]; phi = 0.5 * (phi + Math.asin(ratio * Math.sin(phi))); } var theta = 2 * Math.asin(k * Math.sin(phi)); return { theta: theta, period: period }; } var testState = solvePendulum(L, theta0, t); var refL = 1.0; var refTheta0 = 15 * degToRad; var refState = solvePendulum(refL, refTheta0, t); var testTheta = testState.theta; var refTheta = refState.theta; var test_x = L * Math.sin(testTheta); var test_y = -L * Math.cos(testTheta); var ref_x = refL * Math.sin(refTheta); var ref_y = -refL * Math.cos(refTheta); var forceTangential = -m * g * Math.sin(testTheta); var arrowScale = 0.03; var force_x = test_x + forceTangential * arrowScale * Math.cos(testTheta); var force_y = test_y + forceTangential * arrowScale * Math.sin(testTheta); var bob_size = 0.2 + 0.65 * (m - 0.5) / 2.5; var max_force = m * g * Math.sin(theta0); var max_accel = g * Math.sin(theta0); return { test_x: test_x, test_y: test_y, ref_x: ref_x, ref_y: ref_y, force_x: force_x, force_y: force_y, bob_size: bob_size, test_angle: testTheta / degToRad, ref_angle: refTheta / degToRad, period: testState.period, ref_period: refState.period, max_force: max_force, max_accel: max_accel, matches_ref: Math.abs(L - 1.0) < 0.05 && inputs.start_angle <= 15.1, is_wide_angle: inputs.start_angle >= 45, is_longer_than_ref: L > 1.05, is_shorter_than_ref: L < 0.95 }; }

lesson.title: What Changes a Pendulum Swing?
lesson.description: Compare a test pendulum with a 1.0 m reference as you adjust string length, release angle, and bob mass. Watch the swing path, force arrow, and angle plot to discover what sets the period.
lesson.instructions: Adjust String length, Release angle, and Bob mass to test each factor. Match the reference at 1.0 m and 15 deg, then raise mass or release angle to see what alters the period versus only the force or swing width.
lesson.goal: Know that a pendulum's period depends strongly on length and slightly on wide release angles, while mass scales force and inertia equally so timing stays fixed.
